body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the 69 live gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket — a quiet, unremarkable day by that measure, which is the normal outcome for this tracker. Prices on the two platforms are internally consistent with a gold spot price in the mid-$4,000s: Kalshi's Above $4,491.99 contract for August 31 sits almost exactly at a coin-flip (bid 0.48 / ask 0.52), which is what you'd expect if spot is trading right around that strike, while Polymarket's touch $4,500 in August contract is already priced near certainty (bid 0.96) since gold has evidently already traded through that level this month.

The eye-catching part of the board — strikes stacked all the way up to $5,500 — reflects where gold actually is this year, not a data error. Gold set a new all-time high of $4,524.68 an ounce before pulling back to around $4,450 as traders took profits, and separately remains on track for its biggest yearly gain since 1979, at above 70%. More recently, gold traded around $4,350 an ounce after dropping nearly 2% in the previous session, pressured by elevated global bond yields and persistent inflationary pressures. That volatility is exactly why both platforms list so many strikes above $4,500 — they're re-centering around a price that has moved quickly.

Worth flagging for readers new to the dashboard: Kalshi's contracts settle against a single price at a specific timestamp (e.g., 5:00 PM EDT on a given date), while Polymarket's touch contracts pay out if price crosses a level at any point during the window. That mechanical difference means the two boards can look mismatched without any real arbitrage existing — it's a different question being asked, not free money. Several far-out-of-the-money strikes on both sides also show zero or near-zero 24-hour volume, so any apparent gap there reflects a stale or empty order book rather than a tradeable edge.
headline: No arbitrage found across 69 gold contracts as Kalshi and Polymarket track $4,000s spot price
